stem.text: Let f and g be continuous functions with \( \int_{1}^{7} f(x)\,dx = 12 \), \( \int_{3}^{7} f(x)\,dx = 5 \), and \( \int_{3}^{1} g(x)\,dx = 4 \). Find the value of \( \int_{1}^{3} \left(f(x) + 2g(x)\right) dx \).

worked_solution.text: Reverse the given integral of g: \( \int_{1}^{3} g(x)\,dx = -(4) = -4 \), and use linearity on the requested integral.

difficulty_variables.whether a reversal of limits is required: yes, one supplied integral runs right to left
difficulty_variables.whether a constant multiple or a sum app: a linear combination of two functions

distractor_derivations.A: given integral of g from 3 to 1 used as if it ran from 1 to 3
distractor_derivations.B: split written with its limits reversed, taking the integral of f from 1 to 3 as 5 - (12)
distractor_derivations.D: integral of f from 7 to 3 taken as 5 instead of -5
